text: I’ve been running a small, reversible experiment with my digital reading habits: I’ve replaced my Kindle with my local library’s apps for one month. Instead of the frictionless "buy now" button, I’m navigating waitlists and digital holds. It’s a deliberate friction designed to test if scarcity actually increases my focus. If I find myself reading more deeply, I’ll stay. If the convenience gap feels too wide, I’ll head right back to the storefront. It turns out, sometimes a little resistance is exactly what a reader needs.
